extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical researchers (postdocs/PhD holders) applying to the Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program (HHMI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program (HHMI) for postdoctoral-to-faculty transition support in the biological and biomedical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Research (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be basic science researchers or physician-scientists working in biological and biomedical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research areas listed include biochemistry, bioengineering, biophysics, cancer biology, cell biology, chemical biology, computational biology, developmental biology, evolutionary biology, genetics, immunology. The competition is open to many scientific disciplines within biological and biomedical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Position (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must have been accepted to join a laboratory led by a tenured or tenure-track faculty member at an eligible institution in the U.S., including Puerto Rico, by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a requirement at time of application; research must be conducted at one of HHMI’s eligible institutions (link to complete list provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Commitment (eligibility requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must commit at least 75% of their total effort to research in a postdoctoral training position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimum of two years in the postdoctoral role is required after the grant start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Qualifications (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD (or equivalent) conferred by the start of the grant term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree must be conferred by the grant start date; for PhD applicants there are additional timing constraints (see 'Experience limits').

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / Training-origin rules (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For U.S.-trained applicants: No citizenship restrictions; individuals of any nationality are eligible. For non-U.S.-trained applicants: Must be U.S. citizens or nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page distinguishes eligibility by training origin—applicants should confirm which category applies to them and check official HHMI rules for precise definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience limits (eligibility windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: PostDoc applicants: Must have no more than 24 months of postdoctoral research experience by February 26, 2025. PhD applicants: Doctoral degree conferred between February 26, 2023 and January 15, 2026. MD/MD-PhD applicants: Can have no more than 24 months of postdoctoral research, clinical fellowship, or residency by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timing/experience windows determine eligibility; applicants must calculate postdoctoral/clinical time relative to the stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Requirements (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted at one of HHMI’s eligible institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists many prominent eligible institutions (Johns Hopkins, Harvard, Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, UCSF, Yale, Princeton, etc.) and provides a link for the complete list of eligible candidates and scientific disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous applicants may reapply if they remain eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who applied in prior cycles should verify they still meet all current eligibility criteria before reapplying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Educational and Research Training Record
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of educational and research achievements must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document should concisely present education history and major research milestones relevant to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: PhD Research Description (selected articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include up to three selected research articles describing PhD research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These selections should represent significant contributions and support the applicant's research record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Narrative Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative statements required include: motivation for pursuing a career in academic research; vision for building an inclusive laboratory culture; and how personal experiences relate to values, priorities, and career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives should address both scientific motivations and plans/values for creating an inclusive research environment; these statements are explicitly weighed in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Postdoctoral Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed plan outlining research goals and methodologies for the postdoctoral training phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should articulate goals, approaches, feasibility, and how the postdoctoral phase will prepare the applicant for independent faculty research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Mentor and Training Information
rubrics_metrics.description: A questionnaire completed by the postdoctoral mentor about the training environment and plan, plus mentor-provided CV and lab census.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor materials evaluate the training environment and mentor commitment; mentors must submit materials by the specified mentor deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Reference from PhD Advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: A questionnaire sent directly to the PhD advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reference provides external evaluation of the applicant's PhD training and potential; it must be submitted by the advisor as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document: Curriculum Vitae
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed CV highlighting academic achievements, research experience, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CV should comprehensively document accomplishments and be kept up to date; include relevant publications and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission procedure and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are submitted online through the designated HHMI application portal. Application Deadline: February 26, 2025 at 3:00 p.m. (ET). Mentor materials must be submitted by March 5, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online portal instructions carefully; note separate deadlines for applicant materials and mentor submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process timeline (finalist notification & interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists will be notified in September 2025 and invited for interviews on October 14–15, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan availability for interviews on the specified dates and monitor communications from HHMI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: Scientific contributions and potential for academic research leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed based on scientific contributions and potential for academic research leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess the applicant's research record, significance of contributions, trajectory, and likelihood of becoming an outstanding leader in academic science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: Plans to build an inclusive research environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed based on the applicant's plans to build an inclusive research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives and mentor materials should describe concrete strategies and commitments to creating healthy, inclusive labs; HHMI values training in inclusive lab culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: Alignment of personal experiences with career goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed based on alignment of personal experiences with career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explain how their background and experiences inform their research priorities, leadership style, and commitment to inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program philosophy: 'People, not projects' (freedom to change focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI follows a 'people, not projects' philosophy: fellows have the freedom to change their research focus and follow their curiosity for the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should emphasize the applicant's potential and trajectory rather than a narrowly fixed project; the program supports flexibility across the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral and faculty phase support structure (award expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program provides funding for postdoctoral training and early faculty years: postdoc phase salary support (initial $80,000/year plus $20,000 annual expense allowance; 2–4 years), and faculty phase up to 4 years of research support with annual grant of $270,000 ($250,000 research costs + $20,000 expense allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an application criterion, applicants should understand the award structure and durations to plan proposed training and transition timelines appropriately.
